top_choice_rationale: Optical lattice clocks (Katori, Ye) are a mature, experimentally demonstrated advance in measurement: magic-wavelength trapping removed the atom-number versus systematics trade-off, independent clocks now agree at the 1e-18 level, and the instrument is already opening tests of gravitational redshift, varying constants and dark matter. The two-name allocation is clean and the citation scope is defensible. Twisted bilayer graphene (P002) is a real field-opening discovery and ranks second, though the three-name allocation is less tidy and the field is younger; no award is the least preferred outcome given a well-founded candidate.
recusal_note: Professional proximity to atomic and precision-laser physics (Lund atomic physics, John Hall lab stay during PhD); no direct connection to Katori, Ye or the twisted-graphene laureates apparent from profile.
